description: Add a prominent expired-exam-date warning banner to the student dashboard. When data.student.exam_date is a past date (strictly before midnight today, local time), render a teal/amber dismissible alert banner ABOVE the HeroBanner. The banner tells the student their exam date has passed and links them to /settings to update it. Do NOT show if exam_date is today, in the future, or null/empty.
steps: In app/(student)/dashboard/page.tsx, after the final xpProgress computation (around line 520) and before the JSX return, compute a boolean: const examDateExpired = (() => { if (!data.student.exam_date) return false; const examTs = new Date(data.student.exam_date).setHours(0,0,0,0); const todayTs = new Date().setHours(0,0,0,0); return examTs < todayTs; })();

In the JSX return of DashboardPage, BEFORE the element (approximately line 523), insert the banner conditionally: {examDateExpired && (
...
)}. The banner must: show an amber/yellow alert icon (⚠️ or SVG), heading 'Your Exam Date Has Passed', a sentence explaining the exam date they set (formatted with toLocaleDateString('en-KE', { day: 'numeric', month: 'long', year: 'numeric' })) is in the past and they should update it if incorrect, and a teal 'Update Exam Date' button that is a wrapping a Button with variant='primary'. Add a dismiss button (×) in the top-right corner that hides the banner — use a local useState called examBannerDismissed defaulting to false, and guard the banner render with !examBannerDismissed.
Add the examBannerDismissed state near the other useState declarations at the top of DashboardPage.
Verify the TypeScript compiles: run npx tsc --noEmit and confirm no new errors on dashboard/page.tsx.
acceptance_criteria: When a student's exam_date is strictly before today (midnight local time), the banner renders above HeroBanner.
When exam_date is today, in the future, or null, NO banner is shown.
Clicking the dismiss (×) button hides the banner without a page reload.
Banner uses teal/amber palette consistent with other dashboard alerts (e.g., the IS_UNDER_AUDIT amber alert pattern already in the file).
